author: NorthEast News Desk
body: European shares rose Friday but finished a difficult week under pressure from inflation concerns and higher bond yields. The pan-European STOXX 600 gained 0.5% to close at 639.1, Reuters reported, while France's CAC 40 added 0.8%. Telecommunications companies and banks led the regional gains.

The daily advance was not enough to prevent the STOXX 600's steepest weekly loss since early July. Oil fell more than 3% from a five-month high during Friday's session, offering some relief, but elevated energy costs remained a concern for inflation and corporate margins. Recent central-bank signals also kept attention on the possibility of tighter policy.

Individual moves showed that company-specific news still mattered alongside the macroeconomic backdrop. German online broker FlatexDEGIRO fell 7.9% after the resignation of its supervisory-board chairman. The index levels and percentage changes are Friday closing figures, not live quotes. Investors enter the next week balancing the benefit of the late-session rebound against persistent uncertainty over energy supply, borrowing costs and the pace at which inflation might ease.
dek: The STOXX 600 closed at 639.1 after a Friday rebound, though inflation worries and rising bond yields produced its sharpest weekly loss since July.
headline: European stocks gain Friday but record sharp weekly loss
